purpose: Exact-string applicant aliases for the five mandated deep-case companies in the full-history panel (hist_v1). Roster companies are taken from the store's own company_key mapping and are audited separately; only the two roster-absent companies are resolved here.
source: data/medradar.sqlite, table events, column applicant_raw (queried 2026-11-03; openFDA device 510(k)/PMA/recall + ctgov records as stored)
matching_rule: exact applicant_raw string match only; no fuzzy matching, no prefix matching, no substring matching. A string may belong to exactly one company. Unlisted strings never map.
review_status: PENDING_HUMAN_REVIEW (agent-proposed aliases; every accepted string is a legal name or known trade name of the company or one of its subsidiaries; a human reviewer may remove a string but not add one without evidence)

draeger.reason_unmapped_in_store: not present in config/companies_device.json or config/companies_drug.json, so the store's applicant->company_key mapping leaves every Dräger event with company_key = NULL
accept_exact: Shanghai Draeger Medical Instrument Co., Ltd.
decision_notes: Drager Safety (1 record, 2008) is NOT accepted: the safety division's gas-detection products are not unambiguously the medical business, and the single record cannot move a result. The rejection is now recorded explicitly in reject_exact (was only in this note); no mapping decision changed.
Draegerwerk AG & CO Kgaa is the listed parent; its 510(k) filings are the medical business.
National Draeger, Inc. is the historical US subsidiary name (1991 record).

measured_for_hist_v1.note: pre-audit estimate of ~160 was low by ~40 records; the alias list above is the audited exact-string set

refinement_history.change: added "Draeget Medical AG & Co. Kgaa" to accept_exact; recorded "Drager Safety" explicitly in reject_exact (it was already rejected only in decision_notes)
refinement_history.reason: demonstrable exact-string defect: the registry omitted an FDA transcription typo of the Dräger legal name. The string is unique to Dräger and its 2 openFDA 510(k) device records (2004-06-02 and 2004-08-09; product codes CBK/CCK) had company_key = NULL, so they were silently dropped. Adding it is exact-string matching only (same treatment as the already-accepted Mindray typo "Bio-Meidcal"), not fuzzy or substring matching.
refinement_history.evidence: data/medradar.sqlite events: applicant_raw = 'Draeget Medical AG & Co. Kgaa', source = openfda_device_510k, n = 2, kind = 510k; no other applicant_raw contains 'DRAEG'
refinement_history.panel_impact: +2 candidate events; +1 panel material event after track mapping (the CCK record has no track and is excluded); +0 or +1 pair (see experiments/hist_v1/audits.json)

considered_but_not_added.reason: all 13 rows are openfda_device_recall only, i.e. outside the panel's device-approval sources; adding it cannot change the panel and is left for human review

mindray.reason_unmapped_in_store: not present in config/companies_device.json or config/companies_drug.json, so the store's applicant->company_key mapping leaves every Mindray event with company_key = NULL

roster_company_note: These three deep cases are in the store's roster mapping. Their assigned applicant_raw strings must be listed and inspected for false positives before the panel is frozen; strings judged wrong must be placed in experiments/hist_v1/audits.json as a deny list applied at panel build time.
